issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:main_sa_rate asserts the O(T^{-1/2})+O(N eps_b) expectation bound for Algorithm alg:main_psa under only structural/weight-learning success and \widehat\gamma<1, but the algorithm takes the stepsizes {\alpha_t} as an unconstrained input, and the claimed bound fails for general choices: \alpha_t=0 yields v_T=v_0 with non-decaying error, and constant stepsizes leave a persistent noise floor. The paper's own proof (formal version thm:projSA_rate_template) establishes the rate only for \alpha_t=\alpha/(t+t_0) with t_0>=max{\alpha,1} and a=\alpha(1-\widehat\gamma)>1/2; the condition a>1/2 is needed so that the second-moment recursion sum sum_t (t+t_0)^{2a-2} produces the T^{-1/2} term. These hypotheses the proof needs are omitted from the stated result.

for each $s\in \mathcal{S}$, sample $\tilde s\sim P(\cdot | s)$ and set $\widehat T(v_t)(s)=r(s)+v_t(\tilde s)$.
Assume the SA stepsizes are $\alpha_t=\alpha/(t+t_0)$ with $t_0\ge \alpha$ and $a=\alpha(1-\widehat\gamma)>1/2$.

issues.failure_explanation: The SA stability and rate results condition on a uniform, trajectory-independent noise bound E[|| \widehat T(v_t)-(r+Pv_t) ||_\infty^2 | F_t] <= \sigma^2 (eq:oracleB / eq:oracleA_along_iterates). For the paper's own oracle (one next-state sample per state, \widehat T(v_t)(s)=r(s)+v_t(\tilde s)), the noise satisfies ||\xi_{t+1}||_\infty <= 2||v_t||_\infty, so a constant \sigma exists only if the iterates are uniformly bounded almost surely. This is never established: the stability lemmas (lem:optionB_stability, lem:projSA_stability_template, lem:contract_noise_bounded_iterates) prove sup_t E||v_t||_\infty^2<\infty under the noise assumption, so they cannot discharge it, and no deterministic uniform bound follows from the stated quantities (using v_t(a_{i,k})=0 and sum_{i,k} \widehat b_{i,k}=1 gives only ||v_{t+1}||_\infty <= (1+\alpha_t)||v_t||_\infty + 2\alpha_t R, a growing polynomial envelope, since sum_t \alpha_t diverges). Thus the premise is not a consequence of the other assumptions for the specified estimator, yet the unconditional pipeline guarantees rest on it; the formal end-to-end corollary cor:end_to_end_v does not even list the noise condition among its hypotheses.

issues.title: Uniform oracle-noise second-moment premise is unestablished (and not derivable) for the per-state sampler
issues.why_classification: The premise cannot be discharged from the stated hypotheses (the oracle noise is multiplicative in the iterate and no almost-sure uniform iterate bound is available), so the SA lemmas must be genuinely reworked with state-dependent noise or the algorithm modified—more than a routine local fix—but the repair is contained, uses standard stochastic-approximation machinery, and preserves the method, rates, and advertised scope, so it is moderate rather than serious.
